printed_page_note: no printed page number is legible on this exposure; a continuation sheet's number sits in the top corner the binding takes. Recorded as unknown, not inferred from the ids around it — the sorted filename order is not the book order.
division: S. W. Sherman (as written in the printed heading)
read_pass: the eight middle columns read against the enumerator's own footings: commerce, manufactures and trades and the learned professions CLOSE; mining, agriculture and both navigation columns close at nothing written; the TOTAL column is read on 24 of its 31 numbers and does not close, and its residual is the finding (T-0547)
lines_note: STILL NOT COMMITTED, but bounded and no longer a disagreement between two thresholds. The TOTAL column carries 31 numbers when its components are grouped by eye at magnification — the same 31 the pass before this one got from clustering its ink, and NOT the 28 coverage.json holds "to the nearest line" from an inventory pass. 22 of those 31 sit on lines that a coincident entry in a written industry column fixes independently of any threshold. The other 9 fall in four bands — y824-920, y1005-1076, y2558-2619 and y2699-2772 — where consecutive numbers stand 32 to 50 px apart against a line pitch measured at 58 to 90 px, so each band is either one number written down the hand's slant or two lines closer together than any other pair on the sheet. That is the whole of what is left, and it is a row question, not a digit question: 29 to 31 lines, favouring 31.
no_horizontal_rules: MEASURED ON THIS IMAGE: the sheet carries NO horizontal ruled lines inside the body. A row-darkness profile taken across the empty slaves block finds exactly two strong rules on the leaf — the one under the printed heading and the one above the enumerator's footer — and nothing between them: the largest excess over local background anywhere inside the body is 4.0 grey levels, against 77 to 211 for those two printed rules. The printed form rules this page vertically only. That is the reason a continuation sheet is hard to index, and it is the thing the reading of 33S7-9YYJ-5S could not name when it reported that 'nothing on the image settles which [row] without re-reading the sheet against a row grid anchored on the ruled lines': there is no such grid to anchor on. Every row assignment on these three sheets has to come from the enumerator's own ink, and the only column with an entry on every line is TOTAL.
form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL — number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (ages, names); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns. A blank cell on this form is a zero and is recorded as 0.
closure_note: The enumerator added his own totals at the foot of the sheet. Those printed totals are transcribed under `footer_as_read` and are the committed data on this sheet. Where a per-line reading is attempted it is checked against them and its residual recorded; a reading is never adjusted to make a total come out.

footer_as_read.total_note: see footer_total_argument: the same glyph stands twice in the body, and the arithmetic of the 22 read lines permits 165 and not 105.
footer_as_read.footer_blank_columns_note: the mining, agriculture, both navigation, pensioners, deaf/dumb/blind/insane and schools blocks carry no figure at the foot of this sheet

column_ink_census_note: A per-column ink census over the body, counting pixels 70 grey levels below each column's own 60th percentile, is committed under `column_ink_census` as the structural finding it is: it says which columns were written in at all, and it is reproducible from the image without reading a single digit. The single-width columns are clean; the wide blocks (slaves, deaf/dumb/blind/insane, schools) carry many printed rules inside the band and their counts are dominated by those rules, so they are reported but are NOT read as evidence of an entry either way.
records_note: empty on purpose, and for a narrower reason than before. The per-column readings ARE committed — under column_closure, with every entry's y, and under total_column, by glyph group. What is not committed is a row per LINE, because the line INDEX is the open quantity (see lines_note): a record keyed `line: 4` would commit an ordinal the sheet does not carry. The remaining work is that index and the seven unread totals, and it is T-0565.

pairing.why: a continuation sheet carries no name and no printed page number of its own, so the pairing to its left sheet is a separate reading. T-0539 pairs all eleven at once. Recorded as unpaired rather than guessed.
pairing.page_population_key_note: STILL NOT COMMITTED as the key, and deliberately. footer_total_argument makes 165 the only candidate the sheet's own arithmetic permits, but that is an inference resting on three glyph readings, and a wrong key pairs the wrong sheet. T-0539 should try 165 FIRST and treat a failure to pair as evidence against it rather than against the pairing test.

ticket: T-0564 (the columns; T-0547 split when this sheet proved to need more than one demonstration). T-0565 has the line index and the seven unread totals.

column_geometry.note: MEASURED, not assumed. The vertical printed rules are found by CONTINUITY — an x where at least 60 per cent of the body's rows stand darker than their own local background — because a mean-darkness profile of this leaf reports rules at x 1441 and x 1719 that are a family total and a 2. The eight single-width columns are then named off the one run of seven even gaps that is bracketed by a wide cell on both sides: TOTAL on the left, the pensioners AGES column on the right. The right-hand deaf/dumb and schools blocks stand at the same pitch and have no such bracket, which is what tells them apart.

glyph_inventory.note: The tool measures boxes and refuses to name digits, which is the point: a machine guess at a 4 that is two strokes reading as 11 would launder a guess into a measurement. Its group count for the TOTAL column OVER-counts and the sensitivity row above says by how much — the x-does-not-step-back rule splits a number whose parts the hand drew right to left, and this sheet's 5 is drawn top bar first and then the descender. The curated count below, 31 numbers, is the tool's components read by eye at magnification.

total_column.indexed_by: measured image y, NOT by line number. Committing a line number would commit the row index this sheet does not carry: it has no horizontal rules (see no_horizontal_rules) and its line pitch is measured at 58 to 90 px, so no grid fits it. 22 lines ARE fixed, by cross-column coincidence — an entry in a written industry column stands on the same line as the TOTAL number it coincides with in y, and that needs no threshold and no grid. Those coincidences are named in the notes above. The bands between them are open.
total_column.residual_note: cannot be stated as one number, because the printed footing is itself one glyph short of legible. What CAN be stated is the arithmetic below, and it is the first thing on this sheet to bear on which glyph that is.

reasoning: THE SAME GLYPH APPEARS TWICE IN THE BODY. The footer total's middle glyph — small, low, a short stroke hooking left at the bottom with a faint return above it — is the second glyph of the last two numbers in the TOTAL column, at y2784 and y2860. So the sheet asks the same question three times and one answer settles all three: either the footing is 105 and those two families are 10 and 10, or the footing is 165 and they are 16 and 16.

105 IS ARITHMETICALLY UNREACHABLE ON THE 105 READING. Twenty-two of the thirty-one numbers in the column are read unambiguously and come to 83. Under the 0 reading the last two numbers add 20, for 103, leaving 2 for the SEVEN numbers still unread — and one of those seven, at y1183, stands on a line the commerce column foots at 5, so that family alone is at least 5. Under the 6 reading the last two add 32, for 115, leaving 50 across those seven: a mean of 7.1, which is ordinary.

THE SHEET'S NEIGHBOURS FOOT THE SAME ORDER OF MAGNITUDE. 33S7-9YYJ-24 foots 201 people on 31 lines and another continuation sheet in this group foots 198. 165 over 31 lines is 5.3 per family; 105 would be 3.4, well under this deposit's own 1840 mean of 4.6 persons per household.
footer_total_argument.what_it_rests_on: the three largest unambiguous readings — 13 at y647, and 11 at both y1253 and y2392. If all three were smaller than read (3, 4 and 4, the nearest confusable forms), the unambiguous sum falls to 59 and 105 becomes reachable at a mean of 3.7 across the seven. Those three glyphs are therefore where a pass that wants to overturn this should look first. It is recorded as INFERRED for that reason, and the pairing key below is still not committed on it.
footer_total_argument.supersedes: the pass before this one recorded the middle glyph as unread and would not choose between 0 and 6 "to make a page population". This pass does not choose by looking either. It states what the arithmetic of the read lines permits, and that is one-sided.

closes_note: eleven of the twelve columns and blocks on this sheet close against the enumerator's own footing: commerce at 27, manufactures and trades at 15, the learned professions at 3, and eight more at nothing written. The TOTAL column does not, and it cannot yet, because its printed footing is one glyph short of legible — footer_total_argument is what this pass can say about that glyph and it is an inference, not a reading.
industry_columns_superseded_note: the pass before this one recorded the two written industry columns provisionally, indexed by image y, with commerce closing at 27 and manufactures standing at 17 against a printed 15. column_closure above replaces that block: manufactures closes at 15 (the y2867 glyph is a 3, not a 5) and the learned professions close at 3. The provisional block is removed rather than kept alongside, so there is one reading of each column on this sheet and not two.
